newsitem.title: USA: Calif. panel to rule on Chrysler ban in 20-30 days.
newsitem.headline: Calif. panel to rule on Chrysler ban in 20-30 days.

text.p: A California board will announce within 30 days whether it will overturn or let stand sanctions against Chrysler Corp for allegedly violating the state's "lemon" law, officials said Friday.

Chrysler appealed to the New Motor Vehicle Board after the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) last October banned the automaker from supplying new vehicles to dealers in the state for 45 days.

The ban was imposed after the DMV determined that Chrysler resold 116 vehicles in 1991 and 1992 without properly disclosing to new owners the cars were so-called "lemons," a term that refers to vehicles with chronic repair problems.
The New Motor Vehicle Board told lawyers for the DMV and Chrysler on Thursday that it had reached a decision in the case, and would issue its ruling in 20 to 30 days, DMV spokesman Bill Gengler said.
The board, set up to render an impartial view of regulatory decisions on cars and trucks in California, has the authority to reverse or amend the DMV's decision.

Chrysler called the DMV's sanctions -- which have not yet taken effect because of the appeal -- a "draconian penalty," and asserted that it complied with the lemon law as it was written at the time of the vehicle sales.

Chrysler said it made good faith efforts to keep used car buyers informed about the vehicles they were purchasing. The company also complained about the economic ramifications of the penalty on its 240 California dealers.
"The economic harm to the dealers and their employees caused by this action has been well documented but ignored by the DMV," the company said in its appeal.
The DMV told the New Motor Vehicle Board that the penalty was directed at Chrysler, not the dealers, and that the punishment was appropriate given the alleged violations.

"If the board upholds our decision to sanction Chrysler, it will send a message to automotive manufacturers that sales of lemons without notification to the public cannot be permitted in California," Gengler said.
If the New Motor Vehicle Board upholds the DMV's ban, Chrysler could file an appeal in state court.
